why: Every crash in this patchset (replay-single 0a, sanity-scrub 1c, conf-sanity 0, sanity 60a, recovery-small 23, ost-pools 25, large-scale 3a) is the same LBUG at MDT mount: mdd_device.c:996 mdd_trash_setup() ASSERTION(loh_attr & LOHA_EXISTS). 66475's own diff does not touch mdd_trash_setup; its parent in the TCU series (65291 ps1) crashes with the identical LBUG, so the bug is in an earlier TCU change of the series (the MDT trash dir setup work, LU-18456 changes such as 61977/61978), counted as patch because the series lands together.

bugs.reason: Same LBUG in mdd_trash_setup() at MDT start in both crash logs (and in 5 other crashed suites of ps2 that Rainshadow left as unmatched/ambient): one series bug.

notes: Under-labelling: Rainshadow tagged only 2 of 10 crashed units patch-suspect; the other 8 crashes in ps2 (and many in ps3) carry the same mdd_trash_setup LBUG but were marked unmatched or ambient-no-ticket because the generic '<NODE> crashed during X' signature has history elsewhere. Rule idea: for CRASH units, group by the LBUG/ASSERTION line from the crash log, not the test error; one patch-suspect crash with a given assertion should pull every crash in the patchset with the same assertion into the patch fault. Also, for series faults the culprit is the series base, not the sampled change.

why: test_24 fails in nodemap_test_setup with "nodemap 'c0' already exists": leftover from sanity-sec test_16, which failed in wait_nm_sync because the MGS had default.trusted_nodemap=1 while the MDS stayed at 0. The fault is not 64319's own diff (gss/ptlrpc only) but 67620 ps5 (LU-19921 nodemap: Skip nodemap update and lock revocation, nodemap_handler.c), the lowest change of the GSSIAM series that fails: the series base 67631 ps4 passed all 30 sessions, 67620 ps4 passed, and every series change uploaded with 67620 ps5 on 2026-08-04 fails the same way, while 64319 ps50 (next day) is clean.

bugs.reason: One bug: nodemap property changes on the MGS (trusted, admin, squash_uid) are not applied on the targets, so wait_nm_sync times out ('mgs and X mismatch', 'not updated on mdsN'); the sanity-sec 'adding fops nodemaps failed' units and selinux 21b/21c are cascades of nodemaps left behind by the earlier sync failure.

notes: Under-labelling again: in session d98a7246 the same cascade covers sanity-sec 16 through 85 (about 40 units) but only 23b/24/25a were tagged patch-suspect; the rest were unmatched/known/ambient because the generic 'adding fops nodemaps failed' and wait_nm_sync messages have history elsewhere. Series attribution: the sampled change is innocent; the culprit is the lowest failing change of the series at the same upload time (67620 ps5). A rule that walks the series to the lowest failing change (and checks the base passed) would name it.

why: wait_nm_sync fails: the MGS has the new nodemap value (default squash_uid, trusted_nodemap=1) but targets keep the old one. 67620 ps5 is this change's 'skip nodemap update and lock revocation if no change' rework of nodemap_handler.c, and it is the lowest change of the GSSIAM series that fails: its parent 67631 ps4 passed all 30 sessions and 67620 ps4 passed all 31, while every series change uploaded with ps5 on 2026-08-04 shows the same mismatch.

bugs.reason: One bug: nodemap property updates skipped on targets so the MGS and targets disagree; sanity-sec 'adding fops nodemaps failed' (nodemap c0 already exists) and selinux 21b/21c are cascades from nodemaps not cleaned up after the sync failure.

notes: This is the culprit change of the series fault also seen on 64319 ps49 and 9 other changes of the series. The different property names in the signature (squash_uid, trusted, admin, tenant) look like distinct sigs but are one bug.

why: test_4a reports quota_usr still holding 511/1024 inodes after its files are removed (lfs quota shows stale usage). This change serves quota usage from the QMT usage cache; 4a, 5 and 7e first fail at 68600 ps6 (and its child 69075), never on 68598 below it, so this unit is 68600's own bug. The other units (33, 34, 37, 40c, 64, 78A) also fail on 68598 ps2..ps5 (LU-20354 aggregate MD inode usage for GETQUOTA), the change below in the series, so they are the series' bug from 68598.

bugs.reason: User inode usage not dropping to 0 after unlink (stale cached usage); appears only from 68600 ps6, not on 68598, so introduced by 68600 itself.

Stale space/project usage from the GETQUOTA usage cache (leftover space for uid 60000 at test start, project inode counts 0 or short, fallocate not counted); all fail together on every patchset of 68598 and 68600 since ps2, so one series bug from 68598 (possibly more than one, but same mechanism and same arrival).

notes: alike_distinct: 'Used space(N) for user quota_usr' (4a) and 'Used space (N) for user N' (33) look like one family but arrive at different changes/patchsets of the series, so they are separate code bugs. Rule idea: split a series fault by the first change/patchset at which each unit appears. 40c/64/78A also failed on 67482 (an abandoned earlier version of the same usage cache work), and 78A on 67053 (ZFS fallocate); 33 once on unrelated 68228, so these tests have a little ambient history but not this cluster.

why: After the MDS replay barrier the file is gone ('grep: /mnt/lustre/f11.replay-single: No such file or directory'). ps4 of this change put the md_op_spec bitfields (no_create, sp_cr_lookup, sp_replay, ...) directly in a union with __sp_reset without a wrapping struct, so every flag aliases the same bit: setting sp_replay also sets no_create and friends. ps5 wraps them in a struct and is clean (31/32 sessions pass; ps4 had 7 of 64 pass). This change is the culprit; the series sibling 67604 (client half, stacked on it) failed only because it carried ps4.

bugs.description: all 41 units across replay-single, replay-dual, replay-vbr, recovery-small, sanity-hsm, sanity-pfl, conf-sanity: one bug
bugs.reason: Aliased md_op_spec bitfields corrupt every reint/open spec: replay creates and opens are lost (replay-single 4a/11/17/18/26/27/48/62, replay-dual, replay-vbr, recovery-small 145), HSM state set gets EINVAL (sanity-hsm 1A, 2, 3, 14, 15, 20, ...), setstripe/mkdir gets EIO (sanity-pfl 27). Same code defect, fixed together in ps5.

notes: The patchset also had about 110 other failing units (unmatched, ambient-no-ticket, known, covered) in the same broken sessions; most are very likely the same aliasing bug, so this patchset's patch fault is under-counted, not over-counted. The conf-sanity test_86 timeouts and replay-dual cleanup timeouts are the least certain members. Rule idea: when a patchset passes under 15 percent of its sessions and the next patchset passes nearly all, treat every new failure in it as one cascade of the patch. Fault is wide but one bug: counting units would overstate distinct bugs about 40 fold.

why: The sampled ABORT (log output exceeded 2500 MB) comes from a session full of client data corruption: 'Data mismatch' on DIO reads (119c, 119m, 69), buffered cmp mismatches at page offsets (44e byte 12289, 155f byte 8193), and EIO from lfs mirror/EC resync and migrate. 67791's own diff is osd-ldiskfs only (jbd2 invalidate folio) yet the failures hit ZFS sessions too, so the culprit is the client folio change below it in the series, 58097 ps53 (LU-17916 clio: switch to struct folio): ps53 fails identically (35 of 46 sessions) and ps54 is clean, as is 67791 ps8. All failures are on 2026-09-06 on 58097, 65094, 68661 and 67791 only (the same series).

bugs.description: all 50 units in sanity, sanity-dom, sanityn, sanity-ec, sanity-flr, sanity-hsm, sanity-pfl, sanity-sec: one core bug
bugs.reason: Client folio conversion corrupts or fails reads at page granularity inside multi-page folios: DIO and buffered data mismatches, and EIO in mirror extend/resync/split/merge, EC resync and migrate (which copy data through the same read path). The 'log output exceeded' aborts in 119m/119r/156 are the error flood from the same bug. Possibly two code faults (mismatch vs EIO), but they arrive and leave together with 58097 ps53/ps54.

notes: Series attribution: the sampled change is an innocent osd-ldiskfs patch; the failure set is identical in shape on 58097 ps53 (the client folio patch below it). A rule that checks whether the patch's files can touch the failing path (osd-ldiskfs vs ZFS sessions) would have cleared 67791 itself. ABORT units with 'log output exceeded N MB' should be grouped with whatever bug floods the log, never counted as their own bug.

why: test_57b ('PFL k0!=k1 full' md5 mismatch on a degraded read with OST0002 deactivated) is a test added by 64088 (LU-12668 tests: add EC layout pattern tests), a lower change of this test-only series; it has never run or failed outside this series (all failures 2026-06-03 on 64088..64092). The series' new tests expose wrong data from EC degraded reads (or wrong test expectations), so the fault belongs to the series, not to 64090's own diff (which adds 63a..66d).

bugs.reason: Degraded (one or two OSTs deactivated) EC reads return wrong data whenever the read starts beyond the first RAID set or in a later PFL component: 53a fails at offset 1M of a 12M file while 53b (single 6M RAID set, sub-stripe reads) passes. Same mechanism across all the md5 mismatch tests; likely one reconstruction bug, possibly a few.

Less certain: two-mount interleaved reads during recovery (50a/50b) and recovery after truncate (76a..d) exercise different paths (cross-client cache, truncated parity) and may be separate defects from the offset reconstruction bug.

notes: Mixed kinds in one patchset: the tests 64090 itself adds are patch-changes-test, the ones from lower series changes are patch-suspect; both are the series' bug and the same failure mechanism, so kind should not split bugs. Many units (one per test, n=1) all from one custom session: counting units overstates bugs. Distinct bug count here is a low confidence estimate (1 to 3).

why: With the client mounted test_dummy_encryption, every create in an encrypted dir fails with ENAMETOOLONG: client dmesg 'll_prep_md_op_data()) lustre: failed to setup filename: rc = -36', test output 'File name too long'. The patch rewrites the fscrypt/llcrypt glue (lustre_crypto.h, llite/crypto.c, dir.c, llite_lib.c), and the failures hit every distro (el8.10, el9.7, el10.1, ubuntu, arm) and both ldiskfs and ZFS, only on this change.

bugs.reason: One bug: encrypted filename setup returns -ENAMETOOLONG, so every encryption test fails at its first create (the varied messages 'corrupted in memory', 'could not write with O_DIRECT', 'filefrag failed', 'cannot read linkea' are all downstream). lnet-selftest and sanity-selinux suite failures are cleanup cascades: 'rm: cannot remove /mnt/lustre/d65.sanity-sec_bis/f65.sanity-sec.2: Operation not permitted' (immutable file left by the failed test_65). test_101 (SSK key file not listed in keyring, selinux-ssk sessions only) is least certain but appears only here.

notes: conf-sanity test_37 ('mount symlink /tmp/sym_mdt.img failed! rc=114') is ambient: it fails on master and master-next and on 8 review changes from April to September (ticket EX-14233), so it is mislabelled here and in 56384. Suite-level failures caused by leftover files from an earlier suite should join the bug that left them. Two dozen distinct error signatures in one suite were a single bug here.

why: The 47a timeout ends a conf-sanity cascade that starts in test_33a: setting up the second filesystem prints 'test-framework.sh: line 1839: OST_INDICES: bad array subscript' (the patch rewrites test-framework MDT/OST naming helpers), the fs2 mount fails with EINVAL, cleanup leaves targets running, and every later test fails with 'MDT start failed' or 'target service is already running' (rc 114) until the session times out. Same sequence in all 4 conf-sanity sessions of ps25 (ldiskfs and ZFS) and on ps24, 26, 27, 28, nowhere else.

bugs.reason: One cascade from the broken fs2 setup in test_33a (OST_INDICES bad subscript from the patch's test-framework change): later tests find MDT0000 still mounted. test_37 here fails with 'already running' (rc=114) inside that cascade.
Separate bug in the patch's rewrite of test_160i: 'sanity.sh: illegal option -- -' when it calls changelog_register --mask, which the helper does not accept at this patchset.

notes: alike, different cause: conf-sanity test_37 'mount symlink /tmp/sym_mdt.img failed! rc=114' is ambient elsewhere (master and 8 review changes, ticket EX-14233, e.g. in 65197) but here it is part of the patch's cascade; the same signature must not be merged across patchsets without reading the log. Rainshadow later re-marked 160i as 'covered' even though the failure is the patch's own test edit, so 'covered' on a patch-changes-test unit can be wrong.
